laws.rule: Consuming, producing or transporting alcohol is illegal in Mizoram. Drinking or possessing alcohol there can mean arrest without bail and 5 to 10 years' prison.

Under the Mizoram Liquor (Prohibition) Act 2019, importing, transporting, possessing, buying or selling liquor without a licence or permit can mean up to 5 years' prison and a fine up to ₹1 lakh; drinking without a permit up to 6 months or ₹5,000; drunken disorder in public or drink-driving up to 2 years and ₹10,000.

The Mizoram Liquor Prohibition Rules 2025 provide a permit for foreign tourists (shown with a tourist visa and valid area permit), valid for up to 30 days. Ask the Excise and Narcotics Department about the quantity and where it may be drunk.

layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: The entire area of Mizoram is a Protected Area (Third Schedule, Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025). Every foreigner needs a Protected Area Permit to enter or stay. The Ministry of Home Affairs withdrew the 2010 exemption for Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland with immediate effect on 17 December 2024. Apply online at indianfrro.gov.in (e-FRRO) or the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app; permits are electronic only. Indian missions advise getting approval 30 days ahead if applying with the visa, or applying to the FRRO at least 15 days ahead if already in India. Citizens of Afghanistan, China or Pakistan, and people of origin there, need the central government's prior approval.

layers.authority: Foreigners Registration Officer of the state or district
layers.process: Every foreigner visiting Manipur, Mizoram or Nagaland must register with the state or district Foreigners Registration Officer within 24 hours of arrival (MHA letter of 17 December 2024).

zone-requirements.note: Settled 3 November 2026: a Protected Area Permit is required. The MHA letter of 17 December 2024 withdrew the exemption, and the Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025 lists the whole state. Smartraveller's line that the state is temporarily excluded is out of date (it still links the older MHA FAQ, which describes the 2010 exemption). Nagaland's Dimapur district page confirms the withdrawal (it gives March 2025 as the start for Nagaland).
